passage:
There is a shop in the city that sells old maps. Some maps show countries that no longer exist. Some show streets before tall buildings were built.
A student named Eric visited the shop for a geography project. He asked the owner why people bought old maps when new maps were more correct.
The owner said, "New maps show where we are. Old maps show how people once understood the world."
Eric looked at a map from one hundred years ago. His neighborhood was farmland then. He had never imagined that.
The project became more interesting. Eric learned that maps are not only tools for travel. They are pictures of time, knowledge, and change.
